method: Energy and protein balance (Gifford; Henry and Godden)
asks: how many could the food energy and protein of production feed
counts: calories and protein of production, exports as food, scaled to a land base
what it leaves out: the diet, the pasture and crop pairing, waste
fidelity check against its authors: recipe reproduces 109 and 96 from their totals

asks: how much land does the diet appropriate (a capacity only by division)
counts: crop and pasture land at world-average productivity
what it leaves out: productivity of the actual land, pairing, energy land not set against Australian land
fidelity check against its authors: pasture and feed crop within 3%; plant-food crop not reproduced

asks: how much land would the world need if all ate this diet (a capacity only by division)
counts: land at world-average production, by diet
what it leaves out: productivity of the actual land, pairing
fidelity check against its authors: world, US, India within 2%; Australia +8%; New Zealand -24%

asks: how many people do the crops deliver per hectare
counts: cropland calories delivered after feed and biofuel, exports by importers' use
fidelity check against its authors: calorie shares within a few points; levels 22 to 42% higher (years)

asks: does production cover the human requirement item by item
counts: tonnes of grain, meat and fish against a requirement per person
reading for Australia on current data (m: 40 to 41 (meat), 12 to 17 (fish), 127 to 128 (grain with feed grain)
fidelity check against its authors: production within 1.2%; their balance and the 30 and 77 readings reproduced

asks: at what density does the chance of failure exceed an acceptable level
counts: the harvest in a year of given probability against the diet

asks: how many does the land feed on a stated diet, with pasture and crops paired
counts: land, yields, diet, waste, fuel, fibre, reserve
what it leaves out: trade, variability between years beyond the allowance
